title: The formal companion: the specification gates and the five modules of ADR-0032's inventory
description:
## Problem Statement

The specification has 31 decision records, nine topic files with stable identifiers, and a
conformance checklist that gates an implementation which does not yet exist. It has no gate of
its own: nothing refuses a dangling identifier, a citation that misquotes its target, a
requirement no conformance item exercises, or a renumbering — and the overview records that
"two renumberings have already cost review rounds spent re-verifying what pointed where". Nor
does anything check what a rule *implies* rather than what it *cites*. On 2026-09-16 a review
(`lean-01.md`) found four such defects that every reader had passed: `SEC-1` and `SEC-5` gave
the SSH key two different owners; the relay protocol's summary named an ordering the protocol
does not have; the delivery declaration's presence rule contradicted its own field table; and
`STA-8`'s per-call barrier was evadable by any caller that mints call ids, which every model
does. Each was consistent sentence by sentence and wrong in consequence.

The owner's decision (ADR-0032) is that the corpus's precise semantics — allocation,
declaration presence, relay admission, dispatch and the unresolved barrier, host-pin lifecycle
— are carried as a **formal companion**: Lean definitions and theorems under `tools/formal/`,
on provisiond-spec's ADR-0025 by reference, with the historical traps retained as executable
**witnesses**, and that the implementation is compared against the companion through
**witness files** it emits. The decision is recorded; nothing of it exists in the tree.

## Solution

Land the specification gates and the formal companion in the order ADR-0032 fixes, one
vertical slice per landing, each behind `tools/check-all.sh` with a CI negative control per
check.

First the scaffold (TASKS T30): the seven specification gates ported from provisiond-spec and
adapted to this corpus's shapes, the Lean package under a `TauWeb` namespace with the
`@[req]` attribute, the axiom gate and the index it emits, the Nix shell that pins Lean, and
this repository's withdrawn-identifier table. Then module 1, allocation (T31), with the first
witness file and the emission gate that holds it to the companion's output. Then declaration
presence and meaning, relay admission, dispatch and the unresolved barrier, and the host-pin
lifecycle, each landing as theorems over every input, decided witnesses for the retained
traps, a refused-and-admitted pair for every guard a dated amendment added, and a witness
file.

Authority follows ADR-0032: a formalized clause's home is its tagged declaration; the
requirement keeps its identifier, its MUST, its rationale and its retained traps; the Markdown
stays authoritative for every clause until a rendering gate covers it, and no rendering gate
is ported until there is a table to render. A theorem is never conformance, and nothing in the
inventory gates the first stage.

## User Stories

1. As a spec author, I want a dangling identifier, a duplicate, a gap in a namespace and a
   reference to an ADR that does not exist refused on every push, so that the renumbering
   cost the overview records is paid never again.
2. As a spec author, I want a quoted attribution to a requirement whose body does not contain
   the quote refused, so that "`X` says" is checkable and not an assertion.
3. As a spec author, I want the count of requirements exercised by at least one conformance
   item ratcheted against a recorded baseline, so that the corpus cannot grow faster than its
   checklist without someone saying why.
4. As a spec author, I want a duty assigned to another requirement's subject refused when that
   requirement's own text names none of the machinery, so that a fence protecting an
   operator's machine cannot silently not exist.
5. As a spec author, I want every JSON example and every Mermaid diagram in the corpus parsed,
   so that a fixture with a placeholder or a diagram broken in source is a red gate rather than
   a browser surprise.
6. As a spec author, I want the identifier gate's first run to write this repository's
   withdrawn-identifier table — the retired `SEC-5` rows, `STG-8`, and whatever else it finds
   — so that an old citation still resolves and a gap is a tombstone rather than a mystery.
7. As a spec author, I want every gate run by one script, unpiped, with each exit status
   captured directly, so that green means every gate passed and not that the last one did.
8. As a spec author, I want the ported gates adapted to this corpus's shapes — tiered `CNF`
   items, `docs/design/` JSON, `STA-22a`-style suffixed identifiers — and shown to read what
   they claim to read, so that a port that scans nothing is not a green check.
9. As a spec author, I want a rule I amend to break a theorem when the amendment contradicts a
   property the corpus claims, so that the contradiction is found before review rather than
   by it.
10. As a spec author, I want every "*what this requirement used to say*" paragraph in the
    inventory's clauses kept as an executable witness, so that none of those traps can be
    re-laid without a red build.
11. As a spec author, I want every guard a dated amendment added to be a parameter of the
    module that carries it, with the bad trace refused with the guard and admitted without it,
    so that a proof is never decoration.
12. As a spec author, I want the allocation identity to be a distinct structure of seed epoch,
    derivation version, role family and index, so that two allocations cannot share an
    identity by a type error I never see.
13. As a spec author, I want a failed or destroyed allocation to keep its index as a tombstone
    and no wraparound to exist, proved over every input, so that `STA-22`'s one-index-two-
    machines trap is unrepresentable.
14. As a spec author, I want a seed restored from a stale sheet to use listed identities and
    allocate none until Replace, with that guard a parameter, so that `STA-22b`'s 2026-09-09
    amendment has its refused-and-admitted pair.
15. As a spec author, I want a successful allocate-create-destroy-allocate trace as a witness,
    so that the allocator is not safe merely by refusing everything.
16. As a spec author, I want the declaration's field table to be a total function whose
    totality is decided, so that a field added without its row fails the build, and *presence*
    and *meaning* to be separate types, so that "empty means nothing to check" cannot be
    written for a field where empty means "nothing may".
17. As a spec author, I want the relay's two orderings — no dial before the AUTH is accepted,
    no application byte before OK — to be two theorems, and the destination pipeline to be
    proved to hand the dialer only the validated numeric address, so that this week's
    shorthand defect and a hostname re-entering the dialer are both witnesses.
18. As a spec author, I want harness knowledge and external state to be two types in the
    dispatch module, so that a theorem about the first can never be read as speaking for the
    second.
19. As a spec author, I want `STA-24`'s barrier proved as a derivation over the journal —
    an intent with no terminal record, keyed on the approved machine entry — so that it
    survives replay and session succession by construction and not by an event a crash could
    lose.
20. As a spec author, I want the same destructive action under a new call id, a second
    allocation index for the same approved entry, a planned reset offered after a failed
    append, a `boot_id` change read as success, a resolution observed but its append failed,
    and a disposition read as unrestricted dispatch, each as a negative witness with the
    parameter whose removal admits it.
21. As a spec author, I want `STG-4`'s confirmation predicates and their absence of a negative
    form in the dispatch module, so that "the reset did not happen" can only ever arrive as a
    disposition.
22. As a spec author, I want a disposition modelled as a terminal record of its own kind with
    the outcome unknown, so that the barrier stays one derivation and a disposed call is not an
    open one.
23. As a spec author, I want the host-pin lifecycle to distinguish a rescue pin, per boot, from
    an installed pin, per machine, and to admit an installed pin only from the harness's own
    `ready_to_reset` job, so that a pin from model text and a rescue pin reused across boots
    are both witnesses.
24. As a spec author, I want vendor behaviour, the browser's storage semantics and the
    aggregator honouring a request to appear as named hypotheses on the theorems that depend
    on them, so that a signature shows what was assumed and the companion declares no axiom.
25. As a spec author, I want the companion to emit a witness file per module — its tagged
    witnesses and the bounded enumeration its decided properties close over — with a gate
    refusing a committed file that differs from the emission, so that I never maintain the
    file by hand.
26. As a spec author, I want the bound stated once, in the declaration the theorem and the
    emitter share, and rendered into the file, so that the file's bound and the theorem's
    bound cannot differ.
27. As a spec author, I want a witness file to carry events with provenance and the expected
    outcome at every step, and each refused-and-admitted pair whole and marked, so that a
    core which dispatches early and arrives at the right state does not pass.
28. As a spec author, I want a witness file to carry no `CNF` identifier, no claim about
    external state, no timer value and no key material, so that the file cannot be counted as
    coverage, cannot be read as evidence about a machine, and needs no secrets warning.
29. As a reviewer reading a landing without memory of the session, I want the emitted index
    to say which requirement each declaration formalizes, so that I can check a declaration
    against the sentence it claims to carry.
30. As a reviewer, I want every tagged proof to rest on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
    `Quot.sound` only, with `sorryAx`, a project axiom and `native_decide` each refused by the
    gate, so that a green build means what it says.
31. As a reviewer, I want each check to have a CI control that breaks the thing it guards and
    asserts the red came from that check, so that a red for the wrong reason is never taken
    as evidence.
32. As a reviewer, I want a backticked `TauWeb.*` name in a document resolved against the
    emitted index, so that a renamed declaration cannot leave a dangling citation.
33. As a reviewer, I want a weakened theorem statement or a strengthened premise to be
    reviewed as a semantic change like any other, so that a proof never becomes complete
    because the theorem became weaker.
34. As CI, I want the formal gate to build and gate in the same job as the textual gates,
    under the same Nix shell a developer uses, so that there is one toolchain definition and
    a missing toolchain is a red gate rather than a skipped one.
35. As CI, I want a module under `TauWeb/` that the umbrella module does not import refused,
    so that a proof file nobody reads is not a green check.
36. As CI, I want a gate over an empty index refused, so that a gate over nothing is not a
    gate.
37. As the implementation's author, I want the witness files under `docs/design/` beside the
    credential vectors, read from the pinned tree by tests and never compiled in, so that no
    Lean enters the implementation's toolchain and ADR-0031's boundary stays where it is.
38. As the implementation's author, I want the witness file to supply requests as a model
    would send them and never an already-correct resource key, so that the request-to-entry
    mapping is what my comparison tests.
39. As the implementation's author, I want a conformance item to be able to cite a witness
    file as one input and never as the only evidence it accepts, so that module 1 does not
    gate the first live rehearsal.
40. As the owner, I want the inventory built in the order that lets each module be true when
    it lands — allocation, declaration, relay, dispatch, pins — so that no module proves a
    false requirement to save time.
41. As the owner, I want Mathlib added only in a commit naming the theorem that cannot close
    without it, so that the dependency is never carried by default.
42. As the owner, I want no word *model* in the companion's names, docstrings or glossary
    entries, so that the weights and the companion are never one word.
43. As the owner, I want the rendering gate ported only when the first table exists to render,
    so that the glossary never describes an artifact that does not exist.
44. As the owner, I want each landing reviewed on two axes — against `AGENTS.md`, ADR-0032 and
    the glossary, and against the cited requirement sentences — before the next starts, so
    that the companion is reviewed alongside the specification rather than becoming a parallel
    research project.

## Implementation Decisions

**Placement and authority** (ADR-0032). `tools/` is the one carve-out from "specification
only": the gates that check the specification, and under `tools/formal/` the companion. A
formalized clause's home is its Lean declaration tagged `@[req "STA-22b"]`, one declaration
one identifier; the Markdown keeps identifier, MUST, rationale and retained traps and renders
the clause; until a rendering gate covers a clause the Markdown stays authoritative. No `CNF`
identifier appears under `tools/formal/` or in a witness file, and the coverage gate counts
nothing from the companion.

**The scaffold, ported from provisiond-spec and adapted.** `check-all.sh` running, in order:
the formal gate (build, axiom policy, index, witness-file emission), identifiers, fixtures,
obligations, coverage, citations. Each gate's exit status captured directly. The namespace
table becomes this corpus's: `OVR`, `ARC`, `CHN`, `STA`, `SEC`, `TRU`, `STG`, `CNF`, `OPN`,
with suffixed identifiers (`STA-22a`, `CHN-R1`, `SEC-T1`, `SEC-CLAIM`) admitted by the
identifier pattern. The conformance parser reads this corpus's `- [ ] **CNF-n · TIER**` item
shape and its applicability table. The fixture gate reads JSON under `docs/design/` and every
Mermaid block in the topic files, ADRs and profiles. The withdrawn-identifier table lives in
`README.md` under a "Requirement conventions" section the corpus does not yet have, seeded by
the gate's first run: the retired `SEC-5` rows 8 and 13, `STG-8`, `ARC-23`/`SEC-T*` pointers
(kept, not withdrawn), and whatever else the sequence check finds. `AGENTS.md` is provisiond's
with the Lean paragraph and this corpus's file names; `docs/agents/` holds the tracker, label
and domain-doc conventions.

**The Lean package.** `tools/formal/` with `lean-toolchain` pinned to the same Lean as
provisiond-spec, `lakefile.toml` with the library, the `gate` executable and the `witnesses`
executable as default targets, no dependencies. `TauWeb/Req.lean` carries the attribute;
`Gate.lean` collects axioms for every tagged declaration, refuses anything outside the three
standard axioms, refuses `native_decide` outside `TauWeb.Explore` by the axiom's shape, refuses
an empty index, and prints one JSON object per tagged declaration. `TauWeb.lean`'s imports are
the module list and the wrapper refuses a module missing from it. One module per inventory
row: `Allocation`, `Declaration`, `Relay`, `Dispatch`, `Pins`, plus `Types` for the shared
identities and `Witnesses` for the retained traps. Identities are structures, never aliases.

**The Nix shell.** `flake.nix` on provisiond-spec's, pinned to the nixpkgs revision that
caches the chosen Lean; `nix flake check` runs the same gates. CI enters the shell and runs
`check-all.sh`, then one negative-control step per gate, each against a scratch copy, each
asserting the failure came from the check it targets.

**Module 1, allocation** (`STA-22`, `STA-22a`, `STA-22b`, the credential format's index rules).
An allocation identity is seed epoch, derivation version, role family, index. The journal owns
next-unused per family and the allocated entries with tombstones; reserve is durable before
any external effect; a failed or destroyed allocation keeps its index; indices are monotonic in
`0 … 2^31−1` with no wraparound; a seed restored from a sheet or store uses listed identities
and allocates none until Replace, that guard a parameter. Theorems: no two allocations share an
identity, over every trace; a restored seed's allocation is refused with the guard and admitted
without it; a successful allocate-create-destroy-allocate trace as a witness; exhaustion refuses
rather than wraps. The role-index mapping of the credential format is a closed table whose
totality is decided.

**Module 2, declaration presence and meaning** (`ARC-39`, the declaration document).
Presence is one type — missing, unspecified, specified — for every field; meaning is one
function per field; the field table is a total function whose totality is decided. Theorem: no
path reaches delivered while a required field is unspecified or missing; an empty inbound list
with any listener is a finding while an empty restriction list is not. Witness: the presence
rule as it read until 2026-09-16.

**Module 3, relay admission** (`CHN-15`, `CHN-16`, `CHN-16a`, the relay protocol). The
handshake as a state machine with `AuthAccepted` distinct from `OkSent`; the check order of
step 3 as a total function; the destination pipeline as parse, normalize, classify, dial with
the dialer's argument the classified numeric address by type. Theorems: no dial before
`AuthAccepted`; no application byte before `OkSent`; a hostname never reaches the dialer; a
replayed AUTH fails on its challenge. Witness: "no dial before OK" as one invariant.

**Module 4, dispatch and the unresolved barrier** (`STA-3`, `STA-4`, `STA-7`, `STA-8`,
`STA-24`, `SEC-12`, `STA-20b`, `STG-4`). Harness knowledge and external state as two types; the
journal as a list of events; intents with resource, kind, session and approval; terminal
records including dispositions; `unresolved r` derived; observations carrying provenance as a
type (adapter read, pin-checked handshake, job record, notify event, model text); the resource
key as a parameter (approved entry versus call id); the reset offer's precondition as a
parameter; the observation lattice with ended below succeeded. The principal theorem: an effect
is dispatched only if its intent and approval are durable, the binding still holds, the
approved facts are what is dispatched, and no unresolved call names its resource except under
a durable disposition naming that continuation. Companion theorems: replay yields the same
unresolved set; only an adapter-read or pin-checked observation confirms a cloud-plane intent;
a failed append leaves the barrier standing. Witnesses: the six in ADR-0032's inventory row.
Robot's predicates have no negative transition; "not happened" is only a disposition event.

**Module 5, host-pin lifecycle** (`SEC-11`, `CHN-R1`, `ARC-43`). A rescue pin per boot, an
installed pin per machine; a pin's admission source as a type; connection admitted only against
a pin for the right machine and phase. Theorems: a rescue pin is never reused across boots; an
installed pin comes only from the `ready_to_reset` job's captured output; no connection before
`/rescue/last` fills. Witnesses: each of those three, negated.

**Witness files** (ADR-0032, "How the implementation is compared"). `lake exe witnesses`
emits one JSON file per module: schema version, module, bound; per trace the `TauWeb.*`
declarations it came from, the guard parameters as assumptions, events in from a closed
vocabulary with provenance, and the expected outcome at every step as a projection in the
requirements' vocabulary. Committed as `docs/design/<module>-witnesses-v1.json`; a
specification gate refuses a committed file that differs from the emission. Each
refused-and-admitted pair appears whole and marked. The emitter refuses to emit a module
whose tagged witnesses it did not reach.

**Vocabulary.** `CONTEXT.md` already carries formal companion, specification gate, witness,
assumption, property, theorem, decided, witness file, bound, companion comparison. Marked
region and any lifecycle-module term are added when the artifacts exist.

## Testing Decisions

The one seam is `tools/check-all.sh` and the exit status of each gate it runs. A good test
breaks one artifact in a scratch copy and requires that gate, and only that gate, to go red
naming the thing it guards; it never tests a Lean declaration or a Python function directly,
and it never asserts on a build's stdout beyond the named failure. A red build for the wrong
reason is not evidence.

Controls, one per check, in CI on every push and runnable locally:

- identifiers: a dangling citation appended; a tier removed from an item that must carry one
  (this corpus keeps tiers, unlike provisiond); a withdrawn identifier reintroduced.
- citations: a quoted phrase its target never contained; a `TauWeb.*` name the index lacks.
- obligations: a duty naming machinery its target never mentions.
- coverage: a requirement appended with no conformance item, above the baseline.
- fixtures: a JSON example with a placeholder; a Mermaid block with a broken edge.
- formal, build: the restored-seed guard's parameter flipped, asserting the unsolved goal is
  in the allocation module; the resource key switched to call id, asserting the refused
  witness fails.
- formal, axiom gate: a `sorry` the build accepts, asserting `sorryAx` in the gate's output;
  a `native_decide` outside `Explore`.
- formal, imports: a module file the umbrella does not import.
- formal, witness files: a committed file edited by hand; a witness the emitter did not reach.

Prior art: provisiond-spec's `ci.yml`, whose negative controls are the shape to copy, and this
corpus's `check-install-disks.py --baseline`, which checks a reviewed pre-fix commit and must
fail. The companion comparison in tau-web-rust is its own test with its own `CNF-3` controls
and is outside this spec.

## Out of Scope

- tau-web-rust: the companion comparison, the Rust core's shape, its `CNF-3` controls, the
  README's `CNF-1`–`CNF-4` mislabel (corrected at the next pin bump).
- The rendering gate and marked regions, until a formalized table exists to render.
- The "later" row of the inventory: attest single-use across restart, exposure reach per
  domain, handoff reach.
- Proving selected Rust against the companion (Aeneas): not adopted, not tracked.
- Mathlib.
- Any change to `07-conformance.md`'s applicability table: nothing here gates the first stage.
- Formalizing briefs, arbitrary shell, or anything about a machine's actual state.

## Further Notes

The two panel records under `docs/review/` dated 2026-09-16 carry the divergences the readers
had on `STA-24` and on the comparison mechanism, and what was taken from each. Three things
they left open are recorded there and are not this spec's to close: whether a Robot reset can
be delayed or dropped, whether the aggregator offers an idempotency key, and the preconditions
for reusing `STG-4`'s installed-pin predicate on a general reset.

provisiond-spec's epic `pv-vwe` and its first closed ticket `pv-vwe.1` are the shape each
landing here follows, including the two-axis review before the next ticket starts. Its
`Claim.lean` is the shape of module 4: distinct identities, "the store committed" and "the
worker learned it committed" as separate facts, the prohibited alternative made definable so it
can be refuted, and the witnesses file holding each historical defect as a `decide`.

title: Gate scaffold: check-all.sh, the identifier gate, CI, AGENTS.md, the withdrawn-identifier table
description:
## Parent

tw-formal-companion-nxy — the formal companion: the specification gates and the five modules of ADR-0032's inventory.

## What to build

One command, `bash tools/check-all.sh`, runs every specification gate this repository has and reports each gate's own exit status, never a pipeline's. The first gate it runs is the identifier gate, ported from provisiond-spec and adapted to this corpus: the namespace table is `OVR`, `ARC`, `CHN`, `STA`, `SEC`, `TRU`, `STG`, `CNF`, `OPN`; suffixed identifiers (`STA-22a`, `CHN-R1`, `SEC-T1`, `SEC-CLAIM`) are admitted by the pattern; a conformance item MUST carry a tier (this corpus keeps tiers, unlike provisiond); a duplicate identifier, a citation to an identifier nothing defines, a gap in a namespace's sequence not listed as withdrawn, an id far above its neighbours, and a reference to an ADR that does not exist are each red.

The gate's first run seeds `README.md` with a "Requirement conventions" section and the withdrawn-identifier table this repository has never kept — the retired `SEC-5` rows 8 and 13, `STG-8`, and whatever else the sequence check finds — so that an old citation still resolves and a gap is a tombstone. Pointers such as `ARC-23` and `SEC-T1`–`SEC-T4` (moved, kept) are not withdrawn and the gate must not flag them.

`AGENTS.md` is provisiond-spec's with this corpus's file names and the Lean paragraph pointing at ADR-0032 (the package itself arrives with a later ticket). `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `check-all.sh` on every push and then proves the gate can fail, against a scratch copy, one control per refusal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bash tools/check-all.sh` is green on the current tree and prints a PASS/FAIL summary with one line per gate, exit codes captured directly
- [ ] The identifier gate refuses: a dangling citation, a duplicate, an unlisted gap, an ADR reference that does not exist, and a `CNF` item with no tier — each shown red by a CI control that asserts the failure came from this gate
- [ ] `README.md` gains the requirement-conventions section and the withdrawn-identifier table, and every entry in it names what the identifier was and why it went
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` exists, naming the gate command, the unpiped rule, and ADR-0032's authority rule
- [ ] `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` already names beads; nothing in this ticket touches `tools/formal/`
- [ ] A two-axis review of the diff (standards against `AGENTS.md`, ADR-0032 and the glossary; spec against the cited requirement sentences) applied before the next ticket starts

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately)

comments.author: master
comments.text: Landed: tools/check-all.sh, tools/check_ids.py (adapted to this corpus's shapes: bold-with-title, heading, tiered CNF items, lettered families, 'Moved to' pointers, bare citations), tools/check-controls.sh with ten controls, .github/workflows/ci.yml, AGENTS.md, README 'Requirement conventions' with the withdrawn table (STG-8; SEC-5 rows 8 and 13 noted as rows). First run found STG-8 and the ARC-20 duplicate; the root ARC-20 became a pointer. Two-axis review applied: count in prose removed, pointer cut to one line, CNF-3 and lean-01 quoted verbatim, bare-identifier citations and misspelt tiers now refused, ADRs read for duplicates.

title: Citations and coverage gates, adapted to this corpus
description:
## Parent

tw-formal-companion-nxy.

## What to build

Two more gates in `check-all.sh`, ported from provisiond-spec and adapted: the citations gate and the coverage gate.

The citations gate refuses a quoted attribution — `` `X` says "…" `` — whose target's body does not contain the quote, and any new unquoted "`X` says …" sentence above a recorded baseline. The coverage gate counts the requirements exercised by at least one conformance item and refuses a fall below a recorded baseline; it credits cited ranges within one namespace; it clears its current item at every heading so prose in the tiering and applicability sections is never credited to the item that preceded it (provisiond's 2026-08-31 bug). It counts nothing from `tools/formal/`.

Both parsers are shown to read this corpus's shapes: the `- [ ] **CNF-n · TIER**` item line, the `**ID**` definition form in topic files, the applicability table, and the `SEC-T*`/`ARC-23` pointers that define nothing. The baselines are recorded with a date and a reason, and the coverage gate's report names every uncovered requirement by namespace.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A quoted phrase its target never contained is red; a backticked identifier in prose is not a citation the gate misreads
- [ ] A requirement appended with no conformance item above the baseline is red; the report lists the uncovered identifiers, and `SEC-*` pointer identifiers are excluded with the reason printed
- [ ] The parsers are demonstrated on this corpus: a self-test or the CI control edits a real `CNF` line and the gate notices
- [ ] Two CI controls, each asserting the red came from its gate
- [ ] Two-axis review applied before the next ticket starts

## Blocked by

- tw-formal-companion-nxy.1 — gate scaffold

comments.author: master
comments.text: Landed: tools/check_citations.py and tools/check_coverage.py, both reusing check_ids.py's shapes; baselines recorded 2026-09-17 (24 unquoted attributions counted per file:id; 101 uncovered requirements, OPN-* and tenant-profile rules excluded with the reason printed); four negative controls in check-controls.sh, two per gate, one of which edits CNF-43's real line; two run lines in check-all.sh.

comments.author: master
comments.text: Two-axis review applied (standards + spec, parallel reviewers, fixed point aaedcfe). Fixed: a sentence with two attributions now checks each against its own quote (TASKS.md T12 was the live case; citation baseline re-recorded at 25); a bare range credits its interior as the identifier gate's citation rule requires; the coverage gate's exclusion table no longer shadows check_ids.EXCLUDED; the citations docstring points at AGENTS.md instead of paraphrasing lean-01 A. Left as noted: OPN-* is excluded from the coverage ratchet beyond the ticket's SEC-* pointers, a judgement to confirm; non-item prose after an item in the same section is credited (no such line exists today); the baseline read/write shape is duplicated across the two gates.

title: Obligations and fixtures gates, adapted to this corpus
description:
## Parent

tw-formal-companion-nxy.

## What to build

Two more gates in `check-all.sh`: obligations and fixtures.

The obligations gate refuses a duty assigned to another requirement's subject — "`STA-24` MUST write `x`" — where that requirement's own text names none of the machinery, provisiond's fence bug. The fixtures gate parses every JSON example in the topic files, `docs/design/` and the tenant profiles (no `...` placeholder, no repeated member, no malformed digest or fingerprint) and structurally checks every Mermaid block in topic files, ADRs, profiles and review records, since a diagram broken in source looks fine until the browser.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A duty naming machinery its target never mentions is red
- [ ] A JSON example with a placeholder, a repeated member, or invalid JSON is red; the ad-hoc declaration and the lnrent template in `delivery-declaration-v1.md` both parse (the string `"unspecified"` is valid there)
- [ ] A Mermaid block with a dangling edge or an unclosed subgraph is red; the nine existing diagrams pass

title: Module 1: allocation
description:
## Parent

## What to build

Module 1 of ADR-0032's inventory: allocation (`STA-22`, `STA-22a`, `STA-22b`, the index rules of the credential format). The allocation identity is a structure of seed epoch, derivation version, role family and index, never an alias. The journal owns next-unused per family and the allocated entries with tombstones. Reserve is durable before any external effect; a failed or destroyed allocation keeps its index; indices are monotonic in 0 … 2^31−1 and exhaustion refuses rather than wraps. A seed restored from a sheet or store uses listed identities and allocates none until Replace — that guard, added to `STA-22b` on 2026-09-09, is a parameter of the module.

Theorems over every trace: no two allocations share an identity; a destroyed machine does not free its index; a restored seed's allocation is refused with the guard and admitted without it; exhaustion refuses. Witnesses by `decide`: `STA-22`'s one-index-two-machines trap; the stale-sheet allocation, refused and admitted; a successful allocate-create-destroy-allocate trace so the allocator is not safe by refusing everything. What the module omits (Replace's re-entry to remove old keys, the sheet's import checks beyond the counter rule) is said in its docstring.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every declaration is tagged with the clause it formalizes, and `lake exe gate` lists them under the standard axioms only

- [ ] The restored-seed guard is a parameter with both theorems; removing it is a one-token change
- [ ] CI control: the guard's parameter flipped in a scratch copy turns `lake build` red, and the control asserts the unsolved goal is in the allocation module

## What to build

The witness-file mechanism of ADR-0032's "How the implementation is compared", with allocation's file as its first output.

`lake exe witnesses` emits one JSON file per module: schema version, module, the bound rendered from the one declaration the decided properties and the emitter share; per trace, the `TauWeb.*` declarations it came from, the guard parameters as assumptions with their values, the events in from a closed vocabulary with provenance (operator act, model request, adapter observation, storage outcome of an append, lost response, crash, replay, import or restore, session succession, disposition), and the expected outcome at every step as a projection in the requirements' vocabulary — never the companion's state layout. Each refused-and-admitted pair appears whole and marked. The emitter refuses to emit a module whose tagged witnesses it did not reach. ## What to build

Module 2: declaration presence and meaning (`ARC-39`, `delivery-declaration-v1.md`), with its witness file.

Presence is one type for every field — missing, unspecified, specified — and meaning is one function per field, so that "empty means nothing to check" cannot be written for a field where empty means "nothing may". The field table is a total function over the fields of version 1 whose totality is decided, so a field added without its row fails the build. ## What to build

Module 3: relay admission (`CHN-15`, `CHN-16`, `CHN-16a`, `relay-protocol-v1.md`), with its witness file.

The handshake as a state machine in which `AuthAccepted` is distinct from `OkSent`; step 3's check order as a total function returning the protocol's refusal reasons; the destination pipeline as parse, normalize, classify, dial, where the dialer's argument is by type the classified numeric address and a hostname cannot be passed. The address classification's special-purpose tables enter as an assumption parameter, not as data the module owns. title: Module 4: dispatch and the unresolved barrier, with its witness file
description:
## Parent

tw-formal-companion-nxy.

## What to build

Module 4: dispatch and the unresolved barrier (`STA-3`, `STA-4`, `STA-7`, `STA-8`, `STA-24`, `SEC-12`, `STA-20b`, `STG-4`'s confirmation predicates), with its witness file. The panel record `docs/review/2026-09-16-barrier-panel.md` carries the decisions this module encodes.

Harness knowledge and external state are two types; the journal is a list of events; intents carry resource, kind, session and approval; terminal records include dispositions, whose outcome is unknown; `unresolved r` is derived from the journal, never an event of its own; observations carry provenance as a type (adapter read, pin-checked handshake, job record, notify event, model text). Parameters: the resource key (approved machine entry versus call id); the reset offer's precondition (durable pins and intent); the observation lattice (ended below succeeded). Assumptions: a vendor read reports external state; a read has no effect; a lost response leaves the effect done or not done. Robot's predicates have no negative transition, so "not happened" arrives only as a disposition event.

Principal theorem: an effect is dispatched only if its intent and approval are durable, the binding still holds, the approved facts are what is dispatched, and no unresolved call names its resource except under a durable disposition naming that continuation. Companion theorems: replay yields the same unresolved set; only an adapter-read or pin-checked observation confirms a cloud-plane intent; a failed append leaves the barrier standing; the inference request is unbarred. Witnesses, each with its parameter: the same destructive action under a new call id; a second allocation index for the same approved entry; a planned reset offered after a failed append; a `boot_id` change read as success; a resolution observed but its append failed, with dispatch resuming; a disposition read as unrestricted dispatch; and a successful ceremony trace.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The two state kinds are two types and no theorem's statement mentions external state as known
- [ ] The principal theorem and the three companion theorems prove under the standard axioms, tagged
- [ ] All seven witnesses pass; each negative one names the parameter whose removal admits it
- [ ] CI control: the resource key switched to call id in a scratch copy turns the build red on the refused witness

title: The rendering gate: marked regions for the two formalized tables
description:
## Parent

tw-formal-companion-nxy.

## What to build

The rendering gate (ADR-0032, "No marked regions yet": "the gate is ported when the first one
exists"), ported from provisiond's `tools/check_regions.py`. Two tables become marked regions:
the field table of `delivery-declaration-v1.md` on `TauWeb.Declaration.row`, and the role table
of `credential-format-v1.md` on `TauWeb.Allocation.row`. Both are `match` regions: their cells
carry prose and conformance citations the companion must never emit, so only the tokens the
declaration determines are compared and the prose beside them stays the document's.

Settled by a six-reader panel over two rounds (Fable, Opus, codex gpt-6-astra, codex gpt-5.6-sol;
`.context/regions-*.md`, `.context/regions2-*.md`).

## Decisions

- **The outcome column.** The delivery table gains a fourth column whose single bold token per
  row the declaration emits: `**number**`, `**flag**`, `**nothing may**`, `**none declared**`,
  `**on re-entry**`, a bijection with `Shape` and `EmptyMeans`. Verified collision-free against
  every token in the existing Value and check cells; never a backticked literal, since `` `1` ``,
  `` `false` ``, `` `true` ``, `` `[]` `` and `` `"none"` `` already appear there. The header is
  never compared, so the column title is free.
- **The role table** gains tokens in all three carried columns and backticked role numbers as
  keys: a bare key emits no token and makes the subsequence check vacuous.
- **Escape-aware cell splitting.** Two Value cells carry `\|`; provisiond's `split("|")` reads
  them as column boundaries and the rows arrive with too many cells, so the gate stops before
  reading a token. Split on backslash parity.
- **Placement.** A region may sit in the requirement its declaration is tagged with, or in a
  document that requirement's body links to. `ARC-39` links the declaration document and
  `STA-22a` the credential format, so the rule is checkable from the Markdown with no hand-kept
  map. The check is directional: other documents linking the same file are irrelevant.
- **Its own index reader.** `check_citations.lean_names()` discards the requirement each
  declaration is tagged with, and this repository exports no requirement-head regex, so the gate
  reads `.lake/index.jsonl` itself and reuses `check_ids.DEF_RE`.
- **One label per refusal class**, each printing a list or `none`. A single label can never count
  two, which voids `check-controls.sh`'s "exactly one finding" contract; the identifier gate's
  eight labels are the house style. No trailing `FAIL:` summary, which would itself count.
- **Emission order.** `lake exe render` runs before the index is written, because this
  repository writes the index only on a green run. Provisiond's order is the opposite and is not
  copied.
- **No `--write`.** Both regions are `match`, which provisiond never rewrites, so the flag would
  ship with nothing to do.
- **Scan set**: root `*.md`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/design/`, `docs/tenants/*/profile.md`. A marker in
  a profile is refused by the placement rule rather than ignored.
- **Kind is an inductive** in Lean, and the Python gate still refuses an unknown kind: the JSON
  file is a boundary between two programs.
- **The emitted region text is checked for a `CNF` identifier**, as the witness gate checks its
  emissions. The prohibition is path-independent.
- The Presence rule stops enumerating fields and names the new column instead ("Cite the list;
  let it hold the number"). The two category explanations and the dated trap stay.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lake exe render` emits both regions; `tools/check_regions.py` holds each document equal to
  its declaration and runs in `check-all.sh` after the formal gate
- [ ] A control per refusal: drift in each region, a region whose declaration is not indexed, a
  region whose file its requirement does not link, an emitted region no document renders, a
  duplicate region, an unopened and an unclosed marker, a non-table line in a `match` region, an
  unknown kind, and a `CNF` identifier in an emission
- [ ] One control proves an edit one line outside a region stays green
- [ ] ADR-0032's "No marked regions yet" bullet carries the dated sentence and the placement
  rule; `AGENTS.md` and `CONTEXT.md`'s **Formal companion** widen "renders the clause" the same
  way; `CONTEXT.md` gains **Marked region**; `README.md`'s gate prose names the gate
- [ ] The gate's docstring states what it does not catch: a header row, prose contradicting the
  token beside it, and a key token that is a subsequence rather than an exclusive identity
- [ ] Two-axis review applied before the next ticket starts

## Scheduling

Module 3 (`tw-formal-companion-nxy.8`) depends on this ticket. **No sentence in either repository
requires that edge** — all three round-two readers said so explicitly. It is a scheduling call:
the trigger has fired, the gate is cheaper to port before more tables exist, and the tracker's
frontier is worked in id order, so an edge is the only way to say "before module 3".

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Landed: tools/formal/TauWeb/Render.lean computes both tables' body rows from the declarations' own
constructors (shapeToken exhaustive over Shape, familyToken/credentialToken/secretToken over
Allocation's inductives), Kind is an inductive, lake exe render emits them, and
tools/check_regions.py holds each document to its emission on the tokens the declaration
determines. The delivery table gained a 'What the declaration decides' column; the role table
gained tokens in all three carried columns and backticked keys. Sixteen controls: drift in each
region, a key column, an unindexed declaration, an unemitted declaration, a region its requirement
does not link, a duplicate, three malformed markers, prose inside a match region, an unrendered
emission, an unknown kind, a CNF identifier in an emission, and one proving a sentence one line
outside a region stays green.

Two-axis review applied (4 hard standards violations, 5 spec findings). Fixed: the Presence rule
claimed the column was the only home while two check cells restated it, so the claim was softened
and both cells now say what the check does; CONTEXT.md's Formal companion said the requirement
renders the clause when neither region sits in one; AGENTS.md restated the ADR's rule instead of
pointing at it; README, the gate docstring and the ADR each counted the regions in prose; the
re-check's list lost its empty-list reading, restored as an obligation in the bullet; check_formal.sh
deleted the stale emissions after lake build, so a failed build left both files from the last green
run; check_citations.py now owns read_index() and owners(), which the rendering gate imports rather
than forking, and CNF comes from check_witnesses.py; a 'Moved to' pointer is not a holder.

Left as recorded: the render branch has no instance yet (Kind carries the constructor so the first
one needs no new vocabulary); the header row, prose contradicting its own token, and a key token
being a subsequence rather than an exclusive identity are stated limits in the gate's docstring.
